name: Gallio
overview: Gallio, serving as the proconsul of Achaia, is depicted in Acts 18 as a Roman official who dismissed the Jewish accusations against the Apostle Paul. When the Jews accused Paul of persuading people to worship God contrary to their law, Gallio refused to judge matters of religious dispute, stating that if it involved wrongdoing, he would intervene, but issues of words and Jewish law were not his concern. Consequently, Gallio drove the accusers away from the judgment seat, demonstrating a clear distinction between civil authority and religious controversy.
